name: News green screen
summary: You in front of the story: headlines, posts and charts behind you, your take on what it means.
bestFor: A news story or industry change in your niche, filmed within a day
Reacting to a post, a launch or a report
Explaining what a change means for your customers
needs: One vertical take to camera, ideally in front of a green or evenly lit plain wall
Screenshots of the story's sources (articles, posts, charts)

modes.use: The hook and the call to action: face only.
Most of the video: the story visual fills the frame and you sit in front of it (keyed out on green, or in a rounded window).
1 to 2 s on a headline or a number the viewer must read.

overlaySlots.when: The story header: frame 1 to about 3 s, then once more at the turn.
Each source you mention, with a source chip.
A post you react to, recreated as a generic card.
One number that tells the story.

notes: News goes stale: film within 24 hours of the story.
Change the visual behind you every 1.5 to 3 s.
Say what happened in one line, then spend the rest on what it means for the viewer.
A whoosh or swipe when the visual changes, never two in a row the same, at most one every 1.2 s.
Sources first: the article, the post, the official page.
Log where every image came from.

evidence.why: Seeing the headline makes the story credible and lets you skip the setup.
News reels compete on pace; a new image every 2 s or so keeps the eye busy while you explain.
A clean card is readable on a phone and avoids showing another platform's interface or someone's private details.
Interest in a news story drops fast after the first day.
